en.title: Delete Linked List Nodes Greater Than a Threshold
en.description:
The node values of a singly linked list are given in their original order. Delete every node whose value is greater than x and output the remaining nodes without changing their order; nodes equal to x are kept.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The input is n x, followed by n node values. The original bounds are kept: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤x≤100000, and node values in 1..100000.
en.output: Output the remaining node values in their original order, separated by spaces; if all nodes are deleted, output an empty line. Do not output the number of nodes.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1 3; 5 5; empty text. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Read the nodes in order and output only those whose value does not exceed x; in a linked list implementation, this is equivalent to pointing each deleted node's predecessor to its successor.
